prompt: Write three overloads of a describe method so the compiler picks the right one for an int, a double, or a String argument. Complete the stubs, then run the tests.
explanation: Method overloading lets several methods share one name as long as their parameter lists differ; the compiler picks the overload that best matches the argument's type at the call site. Notice that describe(7.0) prints "7.0" -- string concatenation with a double keeps the decimal point, which is one way to see that the double overload (not the int one) ran. Overload resolution happens at compile time, based on the declared argument types.
hints: All three methods keep the name describe; only the parameter type changes (int, double, String).
Each body is one line: return the label, a colon and space, then the value using + concatenation.
Concatenating a number to a String converts it automatically -- "int: " + 5 gives "int: 5".
